Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our SecOps team reviewed the private-hosted deployment flow and has two gating items before we can sign off: a) how certificates are provisioned and rotated for private endpoints inside our VPC, and b) where TLS termination happens (edge vs. internal termination) given our zero-trust controls.

Attached is our short questionnaire — the answers there will determine whether we need an HSM-backed key store or if managed KMS is acceptable, and whether we need mutual TLS at the LB. Can someone from your side fill in the cert lifecycle and DNS ownership sections?

High level asks:
- Who owns the private DNS zone (split-horizon) and how do we coordinate updates?
- What cert types do you support for private domains (SANs, IP-based SANs, internal CA chains)?
- Where does TLS terminate by default in the Private deployment bundle, and what are supported alternatives?

We'd like a short handoff plan we can present to our procurement and SecOps by EOD Friday.

Thanks Sofia — looping in Dev and Infra (Dev Patel, Karthik) to fill in the technical details. I attached our cert-handoff template to speed this up.

Quick answers up front so you have context:
- Split-horizon DNS is supported; default pattern is customer-managed internal zone with Redwood-managed delegation records for service endpoints. We can also support a full customer-owned internal LB FQDN.
- Private certs: we support customer-provided cert chains (including internal CA bundles) and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM via our Private control plane. We also offer Redwood-managed certs for private domains in Dedicated with KMIP-compatible stores as an option.
- TLS termination: Default for Private is internal termination at the customer side (we present a TLS passthrough to an internal TLS listener) when customers require mutual TLS. Alternative is termination at a customer-managed edge proxy or at the Redwood edge inside the VPC when allowed by policy.

Dev/Karthik — can you fill in the specifics for rotation cadence, automated renewal hooks (ACME vs. API), and DNS update playbook? Also please confirm which metrics/logs we can expose to their SecOps for audit.

Regards,

Sofia, Marissa — technical details below. I'll keep answers short and add an example in the shared Drive link.

1) DNS ownership and updates- Default architecture: split-horizon where Acme controls the internal zone (company.internal.acme). Redwood provides delegation records and a service origin map (see dns-origin-map.csv) mapping service FQDNs to backend endpoints/nodes.
- Update model: customer opens a change in their DNS (or we can open a change request via an agreed ticketing API). We support programmatic updates via a signed API token for automation if you prefer.

2) Certificate types & provisioning- Support: PEM chains with SANs (hostnames) and internal CA bundles. We do not recommend IP SANs for load-balanced endpoints — stick with stable FQDNs.
- Provisioning options:
  a) Customer-provided certs uploaded to customer KMS/HSM; Redwood fetches via our Private control plane over a mutual-authenticated gRPC channel.
  b) Customer-managed ACME endpoint (recommended for renewals) with webhooks to our renewal handler.
  c) Redwood-managed short-lived certs stored in a KMIP-compatible vault for customers who allow it.

3) Rotation & renewal cadence- Recommended: 30‑day overlap renewal policy with automated pre-renew hooks 20 days prior. For HSM-backed keys, rotation is triggered via the KMS API and we perform a staged roll (primary -> secondary -> swap) to avoid downtime.

4) TLS termination patterns- Mutual TLS enforced at ingress: Termination at a customer edge proxy/ingress controller inside their VPC is preferred for strict zero-trust. In that case Redwood serves plain HTTP to the service listener over the private network.
- If customer delegates termination to Redwood inside the VPC (e.g., Redwood edge appliance), we support mTLS between Redwood components and require customer to provide upstream trust anchors. We record client cert thumbprints in audit logs.

5) Audit logs & metrics- Exposed artifacts: certificate thumbprints, rotation timestamps, KMS rotation event IDs, and TLS handshake failure logs (aggregated). Logs are delivered to a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket or to a syslog endpoint.

I'll drop the sample API snippet to the Drive link and include the DNS CSV mapping.

Adding ops & rollout details. Important to make the handoff auditable and reversible.

Rollout playbook (high level):
- Stage 1: Validation in a non-prod VPC. Validate DNS split-horizon, ensure ACME renewals work against an internal ACME CA (if used), and verify automated renewal webhooks.
- Stage 2: Canary in prod: select a single service or subset of hosts, enable rotation hooks, and monitor TLS metrics for 48 hours.
- Stage 3: System-wide rollout with phased DNS TTL reductions — do not lower TTL below 60s for the first 24 hours.

Rollback considerations:
- Maintain previous cert as a standby and keep the previous DNS mapping for 72 hours.
- If using Redwood-managed termination, we support an emergency bypass to route traffic to customer-managed edge via an alternate delegation record we pre-provision.

Security controls & proof points for procurement:
- KMS/HSM integrations: we support AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, and external KMIP stores.
- Auditability: Every rotation request is mapped to an API call id and user id; we can provide a signed export for audits.

Jonas — can you confirm SLA/maintenance window language we should present to procurement?

-Karthik

Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround, team. Below is a consolidated handoff tailored for Acme Payments that you can share with procurement and SecOps. I've also attached the filled template.

Handoff summary (one pager):
- DNS: Acme owns internal zone (company.internal.acme). Redwood will provide a signed delegation map (dns-origin-map.csv). Production updates are via ticket or signed API.
- Cert provisioning: Preferred path is customer-managed ACME connected to their KMS/HSM. Alternative: customer uploads PEM chains to their KMS and Redwood uses the Private control plane to fetch. Redwood-managed short-lived certs available only if Acme permits KMIP access.
- Rotation: 30-day overlap renewals, automated pre-renew hooks at day 20, staged swap to prevent downtime. All rotation events are logged and exportable for audits.
- TLS termination: Default for strict zero-trust is termination at Acme-managed ingress (customer edge proxy) with mTLS to Redwood where required. If Acme delegates termination inside their VPC to Redwood, we require upstream trust anchors and will log client cert thumbprints.
- Rollout & rollback: Non-prod validation -> 48h canary -> phased TTL reduction. Standby cert and DNS fallbacks maintained for 72h after rollout. Emergency bypass record pre-provisioned for quick switch to customer-managed edge.

Ask / next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you prefer ACME (recommended) or KMS uploads (we'll need service account and key ACLs).
2) If ACME: share an internal ACME endpoint or let us provision a mutual-auth ACME with your CA.
3) If KMS uploads: provide the KMS type (AWS/Azure/KMIP) and a contact for key ACLs.

Jonas will follow up with the SLA/maintenance language for procurement; Dev and Karthik will stand up the Drive folder content with API snippets and playbook.

I'll prepare a mutual action plan doc for signatures once you confirm option 1 vs 2.

Best,
Marissa Cole
